title: Lobbyist registry and consent items approved
subtitle: Light pollution rules, heritage property standards, not-for-profit leases, Municipal Elections Act request and a labour agreement with IATSE.
overview: Council approved a Lobbyist Registry By-law and Code of Conduct and appointed Suzanne Craig as the City's Lobbyist Registrar on contract {{vote:m7}}. The registry is meant to make it clearer who is trying to influence City decisions.

The consent report passed without any items being pulled for separate debate. It included a Property Standards By-law amendment setting heritage minimum standards, effective July 31, 2024 {{vote:m4}}. It also renewed leases for the Guelph Youth Music Centre, Royal City Tennis Club and Navy League {{vote:m5}}. Staff were directed to draft rules on light trespassing between private properties, along with lighting guidelines {{vote:m6}}. Council also asked the Province to change the Municipal Elections Act so candidate and donor addresses are not posted online {{vote:m8}}.

Before the open meeting, Council met in closed session. On return, the chair reported that Council received information on a solid waste scales contract settlement, Habitat for Humanity development charges and an Ontario Land Tribunal matter, and gave staff direction on some of them. Council also directed staff to finalize and sign a memorandum of agreement with IATSE Local 357, whose members support live events at the River Run Centre. The Mayor joined remotely, and the chair ran the meeting.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Lobbyist Registry By-law and Code of Conduct, appointed Suzanne Craig as Lobbyist Registrar, and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign a contract for those services.
Staff were directed to create a by-law or property standards amendment regulating light trespassing between private properties, plus guidelines encouraging full cut-off fixtures.
Council approved an amendment to the Property Standards By-law on heritage minimum standards, taking effect July 31, 2024.
Council authorized leases with the Guelph Youth Music Centre (10 years), Royal City Tennis Club (20 years) and Navy League, Guelph Branch (10 years).
Council called on the Province to stop requiring candidate and donor addresses on public online forms, and to have them filed separately for in-person inspection only.

debate: The transcript shows no debate on the agenda items. The chair asked whether any consent item should be pulled for separate discussion, and none was.
The consent report and the by-laws were each passed without comment or opposition. The open minutes were also confirmed without comment.
No delegate concerns appear in the transcript. Discussion was limited to procedure, the closed-session report and announcements.
